brief.headline: Push for ₹28.69 L/yr savings by matching Mars Plastics & Premier Plastic prices — you're their biggest customer at 47.43% of their sales

priceAsk.summary: Match the ₹0.81/NOS Mars price on PP caps (we pay ₹1.08), the ₹1.38/NOS Mars price on HDPE bottles (we pay ₹1.53), and the ₹0.35/NOS Premier price on measuring cups (we pay ₹0.46)
priceAsk.target: ₹28.69 L/yr total savings across all rigid plastic packaging SKUs
priceAsk.basis: We already buy the same items cheaper from Mars Plastics and Premier Plastic — three top SKUs alone overpay by 33.2%, 10.7% and 30.6%. The market asks ₹0.85–0.95/pc typically for 28 mm caps (verdict: MARKET-FAIR), and we're paying ₹1.08 — room exists to reach ₹0.81. Hold them to the prices we know work.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 45 days after receipt to 60 days — they already take 39 days to pay their own suppliers, well above the 23-day norm, so stretching ours is fair
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Frees up ₹16.02 L cash for us if we go to 30 days (baseline benchmark); pushing to 60 days doubles that benefit

brief.financialLeverage: They're a small shop — ₹4.11 Cr revenue, and we're 47.43% of it, so losing us would hurt badly. They keep only 6.0% profit on every ₹100 sold, much less than similar firms (15.0%), meaning price cuts squeeze them hard. They owe 1.13 times their own cash and borrow at around 8%, and their cash is tied up for 101 days (close to the 107-day peer mark) — so cash is tight but not desperate (zone: grey, score 51/100). Use your size to win on price and terms, but don't push so hard you destabilize a supplier who makes half their living from you.

evidence.point: We overpay ₹28.69 L/yr versus the best prices we already get from other suppliers
PP cap: we pay ₹1.08/NOS, Mars charges ₹0.81/NOS — a 33.2% gap costing us ₹14.05 L/yr
We're their largest customer by far — ₹1.95 Cr of their ₹4.11 Cr revenue (47.43%)
They take 39 days to pay their own suppliers, longer than the 23-day industry norm
They keep 6.0% profit per ₹100 sold, half the 15.0% their peers earn — price cuts hurt them more
They owe 1.13 times their own money and their cash sits locked for 101 days (peers: 107 days)

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health score 65/100) — pharma bottles, caps, preforms; top second-source candidate already flagged in our data

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader for pails, containers, pharma — a robust, proven alternate for bottles and closures

alternates.name: Pearl Polymers Ltd (Pearlpet)
alternates.why: Listed PET bottle/jar specialist — direct fit if any of our rigid packaging shifts to PET

risks: They're small (₹4.11 Cr) and we're nearly half their business — pushing too hard could tip them into trouble, leaving us scrambling for supply on short notice
They keep only 6.0% profit vs 15.0% for peers, so big price cuts may force them to cut corners on quality or delivery to survive
Debt is 1.13 times their cash and they're in the grey zone (score 51/100) — not distressed today, but one bad quarter and supply continuity becomes a real risk
No credit rating on file and they're flagged as a small entity — verify their production capacity and financial stability before locking in a sole-source commitment
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, but we're paying ₹28.69 lakh more than we do with Mars and Premier for the same packaging — let's close that gap and talk about stretching payment terms to 60 days so we both win.
